Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.pgsql

Class PostgresSchemaGrammar

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.schema.grammar.SchemaGrammar
org.aristonis.diwan.database.pgsql.PostgresSchemaGrammar
public class PostgresSchemaGrammar extends SchemaGrammar
Turns a blueprint into PostgreSQL statements, following Laravel's PostgreSQL grammar.

Keys, unique constraints and foreign keys are added with alter table after the create table; the connection runs a blueprint's statements in one transaction, so a failure leaves nothing behind. Tables are read in the connection's current schema.

    • compile

      public List<String> compile(Blueprint blueprint, Connection connection)
      Compiles every command of a blueprint.
      Overrides:
      compile in class SchemaGrammar
      Parameters:
      blueprint - the checked blueprint, never null
      connection - the connection the SQL will run on, never null; a grammar may read the current schema through it
      Returns:
      the statements in the order to run them, unmodifiable, never null
      Implementation Note:
      Refuses virtual generated columns before PostgreSQL 18, which has only stored ones, and a connection whose search_path names no existing schema, where every table would look missing.

    • compileDropAllTables

      public List<String> compileDropAllTables(List<TableInfo> tables)
      Returns the statements that drop the given tables.

      More than one statement means they must run together in one transaction.

      Overrides:
      compileDropAllTables in class SchemaGrammar
      Parameters:
      tables - the tables to drop, never null, as listed by compileTables(org.aristonis.diwan.database.Connection)
      Returns:
      one drop table ... cascade over all tables, schema-qualified, by their real names. Types, sequences and functions are not dropped: a migration that creates one drops it itself, or lives in a schema of its own

    • columns

      public List<ColumnInfo> columns(Connection connection, String table)
      Lists the columns of a table or view, in column order.
      Parameters:
      connection - the connection to read with, never null
      table - the full table name, prefix included, never null
      Returns:
      the table's or view's columns from pg_attribute in the current schema, dropped columns left out; typeName is the type's typname and type its format_type text; the generation and identity details need PostgreSQL 12 and 10 and are left out on older servers
